title: 1 Samuel Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 1.

questions.question: What was the name of the man from Ramathaimzophim mentioned in 1 Samuel 1?
options: Elkanah
Jeroham
Elihu
Zuph
questions.correctAnswer: Elkanah
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:1 states the man's name was Elkanah.

questions.question: How many wives did Elkanah have according to 1 Samuel 1?
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.correctAnswer: Two
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:2 says Elkanah had two wives.

questions.question: Which wife of Elkanah had children?
options: Hannah
Peninnah
Both Hannah and Peninnah
Neither had children
questions.correctAnswer: Peninnah
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:2 clarifies that Peninnah had children but Hannah had none.

questions.question: Where did Elkanah go yearly to worship and sacrifice to the LORD?
options: Jerusalem
Shiloh
Bethel
Mount Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: Shiloh
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:3 states Elkanah went yearly to Shiloh.

questions.question: Who were the priests present at Shiloh when Elkanah went to worship?
options: Hophni and Phinehas
Eli and Samuel
Jeroham and Zuph
Elihu and Tohu
questions.correctAnswer: Hophni and Phinehas
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:3 mentions the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, as priests there.

questions.question: What kind of portion did Elkanah give to Hannah when he offered sacrifices?
options: A lesser portion
A worthy portion
No portion
The same portion as Peninnah
questions.correctAnswer: A worthy portion
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:5 states Elkanah gave Hannah a worthy portion because he loved her.

questions.question: Why was Hannah grieved and provoked by Peninnah?
options: Because Peninnah was jealous of Hannah
Because the LORD had shut up Hannah's womb
Because Elkanah favored Peninnah
Because Peninnah was poor
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had shut up Hannah's womb
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:6 shows Peninnah provoked Hannah to make her fret because the LORD had shut up her womb.

questions.question: What did Hannah do year by year when she was provoked by Peninnah at the house of the LORD?
options: She laughed and rejoiced
She wept and did not eat
She left early
She argued with Peninnah
questions.correctAnswer: She wept and did not eat
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:7 states she wept and did not eat when provoked.

questions.question: What comforting question did Elkanah ask Hannah about her sorrow?
options: Why do you cry to the LORD?
Am I not better to thee than ten sons?
Why do you go to Shiloh?
Do you not love me?
questions.correctAnswer: Am I not better to thee than ten sons?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:8 records Elkanah asking Hannah if he is not better than ten sons.

questions.question: Where was Eli the priest sitting when Hannah rose up to pray?
options: By a post of the temple of the LORD
At the altar
In the city square
Outside the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: By a post of the temple of the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:9 says Eli sat by a post of the temple of the LORD.

questions.question: What was Hannah's emotional state when she prayed to the LORD?
options: Joyful and thankful
In bitterness of soul and weeping sore
Calm and quiet
Angry and loud
questions.correctAnswer: In bitterness of soul and weeping sore
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:10 describes Hannah as in bitterness of soul and weeping sore while praying.

questions.question: True or False: Hannah was able to speak audibly when she prayed before Eli the priest.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:13 says Hannah's lips moved but her voice was not heard.

questions.question: True or False: Eli thought Hannah was drunk when he first saw her praying.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:13-14 shows Eli thought Hannah was drunken.

questions.question: True or False: Hannah said she had drunk wine and strong drink while praying.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:15 records Hannah saying she had drunk neither wine nor strong drink.

questions.question: True or False: Eli blessed Hannah and wished that God would grant her petition.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:17 says Eli told her to go in peace and that God would grant her petition.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What vow did Hannah make to the LORD if He granted her a son?
options: She would give him to the LORD all his life and no razor would touch his head
She would build a temple in his honor
She would offer a yearly sacrifice of a bullock
She would name him after Eli the priest
questions.correctAnswer: She would give him to the LORD all his life and no razor would touch his head
questions.explanation: Hannah vowed that if the LORD gave her a son, she would dedicate him to the LORD all his days and that no razor would come upon his head, indicating a Nazirite vow (1 Samuel 1:11). This shows her faith and commitment (also linked to 1 Samuel 1:27-28).

questions.question: How did Eli the priest initially interpret Hannah’s silent prayer?
options: He thought she was drunk
He knew she was praying faithfully
He thought she was angry at Peninnah
He believed she was mourning
questions.correctAnswer: He thought she was drunk
questions.explanation: Eli saw Hannah’s lips moving but no sound coming out and assumed she was drunk (1 Samuel 1:13). However, she explained that she was pouring out her soul before the LORD in prayer (1 Samuel 1:15-16).

questions.question: What was Hannah’s spiritual condition when Eli confronted her about being drunk?
options: A woman of a sorrowful spirit pouring out her soul to the LORD
A woman angry at her rival wife
A woman rejoicing in God’s blessings
A woman preparing a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: A woman of a sorrowful spirit pouring out her soul to the LORD
questions.explanation: Hannah told Eli she was not drunk but a woman of a sorrowful spirit who had poured out her soul before the LORD in prayer (1 Samuel 1:15-16). This highlights her humility and faith during suffering.

questions.question: What blessing did Eli pronounce upon Hannah after understanding her prayer?
options: Go in peace and may God grant your petition
May you have many sons
May the LORD forgive your sins
May you find prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Go in peace and may God grant your petition
questions.explanation: Eli blessed Hannah by telling her to go in peace and that God would grant the petition she asked of Him, showing the importance of faith and priestly encouragement (1 Samuel 1:17).

questions.question: How did Hannah’s demeanor change after Eli’s blessing?
options: She went her way, ate, and was no longer sad
She immediately left the temple and wept
She continued fasting and praying
She argued with Peninnah
questions.correctAnswer: She went her way, ate, and was no longer sad
questions.explanation: After Eli’s blessing, Hannah’s countenance changed; she ate and was no longer sad, illustrating how faith and encouragement can bring peace (1 Samuel 1:18).

questions.question: What significant event occurred after Hannah’s prayer and vow?
options: The LORD remembered her and she conceived a son
She moved to another city
She adopted a child
Peninnah bore more children
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD remembered her and she conceived a son
questions.explanation: The LORD remembered Hannah after her prayer, and she conceived and bore a son, Samuel, showing God's faithfulness to those who trust Him (1 Samuel 1:19-20).

questions.question: Based on 1 Samuel 1:19 and 1 Samuel 1:20, what does the passage teach about the relationship between prayer and God’s remembrance?
options: God remembers and answers the prayers of those who faithfully seek Him
God only answers prayers made in the temple
God remembers only the priests
God answers immediately without delay
questions.correctAnswer: God remembers and answers the prayers of those who faithfully seek Him
questions.explanation: The passage shows that because Hannah prayed faithfully and trusted God, He remembered her and granted her petition by giving her a son (1 Samuel 1:19-20). This teaches believers about God's responsiveness to sincere prayer.

questions.question: What reason did Hannah give for not going up to the house of the LORD with her husband after Samuel was born?
options: She wanted to wait until the child was weaned
She was still mourning her barrenness
She was sick and unable to travel
She had vowed not to return
questions.correctAnswer: She wanted to wait until the child was weaned
questions.explanation: Hannah told Elkanah she would not go up to the house of the LORD until the child was weaned, then she would bring him to abide before the LORD (1 Samuel 1:22). This shows her faithfulness in fulfilling her vow.

questions.question: How did Elkanah respond to Hannah’s decision regarding Samuel’s weaning and dedication?
options: He said to do what seemed best and that the LORD would establish His word
He insisted she bring Samuel immediately
He was angry and refused to go without her
He suggested they forget the vow
questions.correctAnswer: He said to do what seemed best and that the LORD would establish His word
questions.explanation: Elkanah supported Hannah's decision to wait until Samuel was weaned, trusting that the LORD would establish His word, demonstrating respect and faith (1 Samuel 1:23).

questions.question: What offerings did Hannah bring with her when she took Samuel to the house of the LORD in Shiloh?
options: Three bullocks, one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine
Two goats and a lamb
Five loaves of bread and a jug of oil
A silver coin and a lamb
questions.correctAnswer: Three bullocks, one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine
questions.explanation: Hannah brought three bullocks, one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine when dedicating Samuel, showing her generosity and gratitude in offering valuable sacrifices (1 Samuel 1:24).

questions.question: What does Hannah’s action of dedicating Samuel to the LORD teach about obedience and faithfulness?
options: Obedience to vows and faithfulness to God’s promises are integral to Christian living
One should only keep vows if convenient
Faith is shown by withholding children from the LORD
Dedications are optional and symbolic
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to vows and faithfulness to God’s promises are integral to Christian living
questions.explanation: Hannah fulfilled her vow by bringing Samuel to the LORD and dedicating him, showing that keeping promises made to God and trusting Him are essential Christian virtues (1 Samuel 1:24-28).

questions.question: What did Hannah say to Eli when she brought Samuel to the temple?
options: She was the woman who stood praying before the LORD
She asked Eli to raise her son
She requested a blessing for Samuel
She asked for forgiveness for Peninnah
questions.correctAnswer: She was the woman who stood praying before the LORD
questions.explanation: Hannah identified herself to Eli as the woman who had prayed in the temple, showing transparency and faith in God's faithfulness (1 Samuel 1:26).

questions.question: True or False: Hannah’s prayer and vow teach that sincere, humble prayer can lead to God granting the desires of the heart.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hannah’s heartfelt prayer and vow were answered when the LORD gave her a son, demonstrating that humble, sincere prayer aligns with God’s will and leads to His blessings (1 Samuel 1:10-11, 19-20).

questions.question: True or False: Eli’s initial misunderstanding of Hannah’s prayer shows that spiritual leaders can sometimes misinterpret the actions of others.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Eli thought Hannah was drunk because he saw her lips moving without sound, showing that even spiritual leaders can err and need to listen carefully (1 Samuel 1:12-14).

questions.question: True or False: Hannah immediately took Samuel to the LORD after his birth without any delay.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hannah waited until Samuel was weaned before taking him to the LORD, showing patience and careful fulfillment of her vow (1 Samuel 1:22-23).

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 1.

questions.question: What was Hannah's condition when Elkanah and all his house went up to offer the yearly sacrifice?
options: She went with them
She stayed behind because she was pregnant
She did not go up because she was fasting
She did not go up because the child was not yet weaned
questions.correctAnswer: She did not go up because the child was not yet weaned
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:22 states that Hannah did not go up with Elkanah because she said she would not go until the child was weaned.

questions.question: How did Elkanah respond to Hannah's decision to stay until the child was weaned?
options: He insisted she come immediately
He forbade her from delaying
He consented and said to do what seemed good
He was angry and silent
questions.correctAnswer: He consented and said to do what seemed good
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:23 records Elkanah telling Hannah to do what seemed good and to tarry until she had weaned the child.

questions.question: What offerings did Hannah bring with her when she took Samuel to the house of the LORD?
options: One bullock, two ephahs of flour, and a bottle of oil
Three bullocks, one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine
Two bullocks, one ephah of barley, and a bottle of wine
Four bullocks, two ephahs of flour, and a bottle of wine
questions.correctAnswer: Three bullocks, one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:24 specifies the gifts as three bullocks, one ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine.

questions.question: Who received the child Samuel at the house of the LORD?
options: Elkanah
Eli
Hophni
Phinehas
questions.correctAnswer: Eli
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:25 states that they slew a bullock and brought the child to Eli.

questions.question: What was Hannah's declaration to Eli upon bringing Samuel to the temple?
options: She was a woman who had prayed to the LORD
She requested Samuel to be made a priest
She asked Eli to adopt Samuel
She declared Samuel was destined to be king
questions.correctAnswer: She was a woman who had prayed to the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:26 shows Hannah telling Eli that she was the woman who stood praying to the LORD there.

questions.question: What reason did Hannah give for the naming of her son Samuel?
options: Because he was born in Shiloh
Because she had asked the LORD for him
Because he was the firstborn
Because he was destined to be a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: Because she had asked the LORD for him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:20 records Hannah saying she called his name Samuel, meaning 'Because I have asked him of the LORD.'

questions.question: What vow did Hannah make concerning her son Samuel?
options: That he would be a king
That he would serve the LORD all his life and no razor would touch his head
That he would marry within the tribe of Ephraim
That he would never leave Ramah
questions.correctAnswer: That he would serve the LORD all his life and no razor would touch his head
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:11 records Hannah’s vow that if God gave her a man child, she would give him to the LORD all his days and no razor would come upon his head.

questions.question: True or False: Hannah’s adversary Peninnah provoked her to make her fret because the LORD had shut up her womb.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:6 explains that Peninnah provoked Hannah sorely to make her fret because the LORD had shut up her womb.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Hannah’s prayer and vow, emphasizing her petition and dedication of Samuel?
options: Chiasmus
Metaphor
Parable
Simile
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: The structure of Hannah’s prayer and vow (1 Samuel 1:10-11) shows chiasmus, centering on her petition and dedication, a common Hebrew literary device.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'vow' as used in Hannah’s prayer (1 Samuel 1:11)?
options: A solemn promise to God
A casual request
A ritual sacrifice
A joyful song
questions.correctAnswer: A solemn promise to God
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'vow' (neder) means a solemn promise or pledge to God, as Hannah makes in 1 Samuel 1:11.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of a barren woman praying for a child as found in 1 Samuel 1?
options: Genesis 30:1-2
Exodus 20:12
Leviticus 19:18
Numbers 6:24-26
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 30:1-2
questions.explanation: Genesis 30:1-2 also narrates Rachel’s barrenness and prayer for a child, paralleling Hannah’s story in 1 Samuel 1.

questions.question: How does Hannah’s dedication of Samuel foreshadow the Nazarite vow found later in the Bible?
options: Samuel would never eat meat
Samuel would have long hair and be dedicated to God from birth
Samuel would lead the Israelites into battle
Samuel would become a king
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel would have long hair and be dedicated to God from birth
questions.explanation: Hannah’s vow that no razor should touch Samuel’s head (1 Samuel 1:11) foreshadows the Nazarite vow described in Numbers 6:1-21, indicating lifelong dedication to God.

questions.question: True or False: Eli initially thought Hannah was drunk when he saw her praying silently with moving lips.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:13-14 shows Eli mistaking Hannah’s silent prayer for drunkenness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God answering the prayer of a barren woman as seen in Hannah’s story?
options: Luke 1:5-25
Acts 2:1-4
Hebrews 11:1-3
questions.correctAnswer: Luke 1:5-25
questions.explanation: Luke 1:5-25 narrates Elizabeth’s barrenness and God’s answer to her prayer, paralleling Hannah’s experience in 1 Samuel 1.

questions.question: What was the significance of Eli’s blessing to Hannah after her prayer at the temple?
options: It showed Eli’s approval and hope for God’s fulfillment
It was a formal priestly curse
It was a demand for payment
It was a dismissal
questions.correctAnswer: It showed Eli’s approval and hope for God’s fulfillment
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 1:17, Eli blesses Hannah, saying 'Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition,' showing priestly approval and hope.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 1:5 reveal about God's sovereignty in human fertility and blessing?
options: God gave Hannah a worthy portion despite her barrenness
God shut up Hannah’s womb, showing His control over life
God favored Peninnah because she had children
God punished Hannah for her sins by closing her womb
questions.correctAnswer: God shut up Hannah’s womb, showing His control over life
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:5 states that 'the LORD had shut up her womb,' demonstrating God's sovereign power over fertility and the ability to bless or withhold children according to His will. This reveals divine control over life and blessing rather than human merit.

questions.question: How does Hannah’s vow in 1 Samuel 1:11 reflect the doctrine of dedication and consecration to God?
options: She promised to offer a sacrifice for a son
She vowed to give her son to the LORD all his life with no razor on his head
She promised to donate wealth if God answered her
She vowed to abstain from wine and strong drink
questions.correctAnswer: She vowed to give her son to the LORD all his life with no razor on his head
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 1:11, Hannah vows that if God grants her a son, she will dedicate him to the LORD for life, and no razor shall touch his head. This reflects the doctrine of consecration, where individuals or their offspring are set apart wholly for God's service, akin to Nazarite vows (cf. Numbers 6).

questions.question: What does Eli’s initial misunderstanding of Hannah’s prayer in 1 Samuel 1:13-14 reveal about human limitations in discerning divine interaction?
options: He immediately recognized her as a prophetess
He thought she was drunk because he could not perceive her silent prayer
He joined her in prayer enthusiastically
He ignored her completely
questions.correctAnswer: He thought she was drunk because he could not perceive her silent prayer
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:13-14 shows Eli misjudging Hannah’s silent, heartfelt prayer as drunkenness. This highlights human fallibility in interpreting spiritual matters, emphasizing that divine encounters may not always be outwardly visible or understood by others, pointing to the mystery of God’s workings.

questions.question: How does the narrative in 1 Samuel 1:20 contribute to the biblical theology of God answering prayer in His timing?
options: It teaches that God answers all prayers immediately
It shows God responding after a time with the gift of Samuel
It suggests prayers are only answered if repeated often
It indicates that God ignores the prayers of the barren
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God responding after a time with the gift of Samuel
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:20 records that Hannah conceived and bore Samuel after a period of prayer and waiting, affirming that God answers prayer in His sovereign timing, often after testing faith and patience, consistent with broader biblical teaching (e.g., Psalm 27:14).

questions.question: Which divine attribute does God demonstrate by remembering Hannah and granting her request, as seen in 1 Samuel 1:19-20?
options: Immutability
Omnipresence
Faithfulness and mercy
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness and mercy
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 1:19-20, the LORD 'remembered her' and granted her petition, revealing His faithfulness to His promises and mercy toward His people. This shows God's compassionate nature and steadfast commitment to those who call on Him.

questions.question: What theological insight does the contrast between Peninnah and Hannah in 1 Samuel 1:2-6 provide about human suffering and divine testing?
options: God punishes the wicked with barrenness
Human suffering can be a form of divine testing and refinement
Only the favored receive children
Jealousy is always sinful
questions.correctAnswer: Human suffering can be a form of divine testing and refinement
questions.explanation: Verses 1 Samuel 1:2-6 show Hannah’s barrenness and Peninnah’s provocation. Hannah’s suffering is not punishment but a trial that tests and deepens her faith, illustrating how God can use human affliction for sanctification and preparation for greater purposes (cf. James 1:2-4).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 1:3-4 illustrate the importance of worship and sacrifice in covenant relationship with God?
options: Elkanah neglected worship and focused on family
Annual worship and sacrifice at Shiloh are acts of covenant faithfulness
Worship was optional and irregular in Israel
Sacrifices were only for priests
questions.correctAnswer: Annual worship and sacrifice at Shiloh are acts of covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 1:3-4 describe Elkanah’s yearly pilgrimage to worship and sacrifice at Shiloh, underscoring the role of regular worship and sacrifice as integral to Israel’s covenant relationship with God, expressing dependence, obedience, and communal identity (cf. Deuteronomy 16).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about prayer and divine response do 1 Samuel 1:10-11 and 1 Samuel 1:27-28 teach?
options: Prayer is powerless unless accompanied by offerings
God answers prayer and calls for lifelong dedication in response
Only public prayers are effective
God answers only after priests intercede
questions.correctAnswer: God answers prayer and calls for lifelong dedication in response
questions.explanation: These verses show Hannah’s earnest prayer (1:10-11) and her subsequent dedication of Samuel to God (1:27-28), teaching that God not only hears and answers sincere prayer but also calls for a life consecrated to Him as a response of faith and gratitude.

questions.question: How does the episode of Hannah’s prayer and vow (1 Samuel 1:10-11) foreshadow Christ’s role in redemptive history?
options: Christ is the son given by God in answer to prayer
Hannah’s vow predicts Christ’s atoning sacrifice
Samuel is a direct incarnation of Christ
There is no foreshadowing of Christ here
questions.correctAnswer: Christ is the son given by God in answer to prayer
questions.explanation: Hannah’s prayer for a son and vow to dedicate him to God (1 Samuel 1:10-11) typologically foreshadow the ultimate Son given by God—Jesus Christ—who is the true answer to humanity’s petitions and is dedicated entirely to God’s redemptive mission (cf. John 3:16).

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 1:8 teach about human comfort amid suffering and the value of children in ancient Israel?
options: Children were considered a curse
Elkanah’s words show that children were valued as blessings
Elkanah dismissed Hannah’s sorrow
Suffering was seen as proof of divine rejection
questions.correctAnswer: Elkanah’s words show that children were valued as blessings
questions.explanation: Elkanah’s consoling question in 1 Samuel 1:8—'Am not I better to thee than ten sons?'—reflects the high cultural value placed on children as blessings and the pain of barrenness. It also suggests that spousal love and support are themselves a form of blessing amid suffering.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 1 Samuel 1:11 shows superstition in Hannah’s vow. What does 1 Samuel 1:11-17 actually teach about prayer and God’s response to human sorrow?
options: It teaches that vows are magical formulas to manipulate God
It reveals sincere, faithful prayer and God’s compassionate hearing
It encourages drunkenness as a way to pray
It shows God ignores prayer when made silently
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals sincere, faithful prayer and God’s compassionate hearing
questions.explanation: Verses 11-17 show Hannah’s heartfelt, sober prayer and vow, her deep sorrow, and Eli’s blessing, teaching that prayer is a sincere pouring out of the soul before God who compassionately hears and responds, not superstition or manipulation.

questions.question: What combined theological insight on sanctification and God’s providential care do 1 Samuel 1:22-24 and 1 Samuel 1:28 convey?
options: Sanctification is optional for God’s servants
God’s providence leads to lifelong dedication and service
Children should always remain at home
God demands sacrifices without personal commitment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence leads to lifelong dedication and service
questions.explanation: These verses show Hannah’s purposeful dedication of Samuel to God after weaning (1:22-24) and her statement that he is lent to the LORD for life (1:28), teaching that God’s providential blessing entails a life of sanctification and committed service to Him.

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth about God’s knowledge and remembrance is illustrated by 1 Samuel 1:19 and 1 Samuel 1:20 in the context of Hannah’s barrenness and answered prayer?
options: God forgets the prayers of the lowly
God’s remembrance signifies active, redemptive intervention
God only remembers the righteous
God answers only public prayers
questions.correctAnswer: God’s remembrance signifies active, redemptive intervention
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the LORD remembered her' in 1 Samuel 1:19-20 indicates God’s intimate knowledge and active intervention in human affairs, especially in reversing barrenness and granting life, affirming the doctrine of God’s providential care and covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What narrative arc does 1 Samuel 1:24-25 begin that is crucial to the unfolding redemptive history of Israel?
options: The establishment of a permanent priesthood at Shiloh
The birth and dedication of Samuel, a prophetic forerunner of the monarchy and Messiah
The destruction of Shiloh by the Philistines
The end of the sacrificial system
questions.correctAnswer: The birth and dedication of Samuel, a prophetic forerunner of the monarchy and Messiah
questions.explanation: Verses 24-25 mark the presentation of Samuel to Eli, beginning the narrative of Samuel as a prophet and judge who anoints Israel’s first kings, foreshadowing Christ as the ultimate Prophet and King in redemptive history (cf. Deuteronomy 18:15).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His response to Hannah’s prayer and vow as seen in 1 Samuel 1:17?
options: God’s justice in punishing the wicked
God’s peace-giving and granting of petitions
God’s wrath against sinners
God’s indifference to human prayer
questions.correctAnswer: God’s peace-giving and granting of petitions
questions.explanation: Eli’s blessing in 1 Samuel 1:17—'Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition'—reflects God’s attribute as the giver of peace and the one who answers faithful prayer, emphasizing His merciful and gracious nature.
